newsitem.title: INDIA: India keen on sunflower oil imports.
newsitem.headline: India keen on sunflower oil imports.

text.p: A sharp rise in Malaysian palm olein prices is making Indian edible oil importers opt for sunflower oil from Argentina and the U.S., industry officials and traders said on Wednesday.
"Buyers are preferring sunflower over palm olein imports as Malaysian palm olein prices have shot up sharply," Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.
Industry officials said Malaysian palm olein was currently quoted at $630 per tonne CIF, up from around $590 a week ago.
"Palm olein prices have risen sharply in the last five to six days," O.P. Goenka, president of Central Organisation of Oil Industry and Trade, told Reuters.
Traders said palm olein was currently quoted at 29,000 rupees per tonne in domestic markets, against 28,300 rupees in the past week. Sunflower oil was also quoted at around 29,000 rupees per tonne.
Groundnut oil was steady at 35,000 rupees per tonne. Soyoil was at 29,000 rupees against 28,000 a week ago.
Shah said India was expected to import around 150,000 tonnes of sunflower oil during January and March. Industry officials put palm olein imports in the same period at about 60,000 tonnes.
Shah said two shipments of sunflower oil, one with 10,000 tonnes and the other with 5,000, had reached Bombay.
Traders said around 100 tonnes of groundnut oil were currently arriving in the Bombay markets daily.
They said soybean arrivals had fallen to around 50,000 bags (one bag = 70 kg) per day from 70,000 a week ago in the central Indian markets, the hub of India's soybean industry.
Arrivals of groundnuts had risen to around 100,000 bags in the western state of Gujarat against 60,000 in the past week, traders said.
